acceptance: The exact implementation changes only crates/morize-core/src/identity.rs, crates/morize-core/src/bounded.rs, and crates/morize-core/src/bounded_collection.rs.
For each changed file, all production source before its existing #[cfg(test)] module is byte-for-byte identical to the exact WorkPacket baseline.

The durable-ID property matrix deterministically exercises canonical from-bytes -> text -> parse round trips across all 256 repeated-byte patterns for every durable ID type, with lowercase canonical text preserved.

The durable-ID parser matrix deterministically verifies that representative non-canonical ASCII bytes are rejected at every text byte position without changing the existing error taxonomy or canonical-length contract.

The BoundedUtf8 property matrix covers multiple const byte limits and a fixed corpus containing empty, ASCII, multibyte, and decomposed Unicode values, proving acceptance iff byte length is within the limit, exact byte preservation on success, and exact TooLong counts on rejection.

The BoundedVec property matrix covers multiple const item limits and deterministic vector lengths, proving acceptance iff item count is within the limit, order/value preservation on success, and lossless rejected-value recovery on failed construction and push.
The property matrices use no randomness, wall clock, network, model, filesystem fixture, environment-dependent input, or third-party test framework.
cargo fmt --all -- --check passes on the exact implementation head.
cargo check --workspace --all-targets --offline passes on the exact implementation head.
cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --offline -- -D warnings passes on the exact implementation head.
cargo test --workspace --all-targets --offline passes on the exact implementation head and executes the new deterministic property matrices.
Cargo manifests and Cargo.lock are unchanged; no runtime, build, dev, or test dependency is added.
GitHub Actions passes Ubuntu, macOS, and Windows on the exact implementation head before acceptance.

An independent semantic reviewer reviews the exact implementation head for deterministic property coverage, preservation of production code, prerequisite identity, scope containment, absence of fuzz-engine/randomness/dependency claims, and required evidence.
ADR-0004 proof prerequisites SG-000012, SG-000013, and SG-000014 revalidate against the exact WorkPacket baseline before execution.

method.control: Implementation is test-only inside the existing #[cfg(test)] modules of identity.rs, bounded.rs, and bounded_collection.rs. Production items before those test modules must remain byte-for-byte unchanged. No new API, runtime behavior, random generator, fuzz engine, dependency, serialization, persistence, or domain semantics are authorized.
method.review_separation: An independent semantic reviewer must review the exact implementation head for property-matrix fidelity, deterministic bounded execution, exact prerequisite identity, preservation of production code, absence of dependencies/randomness/fuzz-engine claims, scope containment, and required evidence separately from the implementing agent before acceptance.
method.rollback: Revert the test-only SG-000023 implementation commit. Production behavior and persisted/user data are unaffected because this Grain changes only existing test modules.

minimality.rationale: Test-only deterministic matrices over the three already-proven core primitives are the narrowest P1 verification increment that increases parser/invariant coverage without inventing domain schemas or adding fuzz tooling, randomness, dependencies, timestamps, digests, serialization, or persistence.

requirements: The implementation must remain test-only and deterministic; it must not weaken fail-closed parser/bounds behavior, disclose hidden data, alter production semantics, or claim that deterministic matrices are equivalent to a true fuzz campaign.

outcome: morize-core strengthens the already-implemented durable-ID parser and bounded UTF-8/ordered-collection invariants with dependency-free deterministic property-style test matrices, without changing production API or behavior and without introducing a fuzz engine, randomness, serialization, persistence, or new dependencies.
rationale: P1 requires property and fuzz tests for parsers/invariants. SG-000012, SG-000013, and SG-000014 already define the deterministic ID, bounded UTF-8, and bounded ordered-collection contracts. This Grain adds a reproducible property-style matrix over those existing contracts as the smallest safe next verification slice while leaving a true fuzz harness to a later dedicated Grain.

risk.recovery: Revert the test-only SG-000023 implementation commit. Production behavior and persisted/user data are unaffected because this Grain changes only existing test modules.

scope_in: Extend only the existing #[cfg(test)] module in crates/morize-core/src/identity.rs with a deterministic property matrix that exercises canonical durable-ID round trips over a broad fixed byte corpus and rejects non-canonical ASCII parser input without changing the ID parser contract.

Extend only the existing #[cfg(test)] module in crates/morize-core/src/bounded.rs with deterministic corpus/limit matrices proving BoundedUtf8 accepts exactly values whose UTF-8 byte length is within the selected const bound, preserves accepted bytes exactly, and reports exact TooLong byte counts without truncation or normalization.

Extend only the existing #[cfg(test)] module in crates/morize-core/src/bounded_collection.rs with deterministic item-count/limit matrices proving construction accepts exactly values within the selected const bound, preserves accepted order/values, and returns rejected values unchanged when construction or push exceeds the bound.
Keep every property matrix deterministic, finite, standard-library-only, and reproducible on Linux, macOS, and Windows.
scope_out: Any production code or public API change, including new constructors, parsers, error variants, traits, exports, normalization, serialization, persistence, timestamp, digest, policy, or domain behavior.
Randomized testing, nondeterministic seeds, proptest/quickcheck, cargo-fuzz/libFuzzer/AFL or any other fuzz engine or corpus infrastructure; those require a later dedicated Grain.
Any runtime, build, dev, or test dependency; Cargo.toml files and Cargo.lock must remain unchanged.
Any claim that this deterministic property matrix completes the separate P1 fuzz-testing requirement.
title: Add deterministic core property matrices
